status.en: 456 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 39% more than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.

summary.en: The Cockroach Janta party leader was arrested and other party leaders were jailed for violating a protest site ban, indicating ongoing repression of dissent. In Haryana, two individuals were detained for allegedly attacking a bus bound for Srinagar, prompting condemnation from Kashmir leaders. In Manipur, Kuki militants announced a shutdown of a key highway after attacks on villages, fifteen houses were set on fire in Kamjong district, and one person was killed in clashes in Thoubal district, with curfews imposed. 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Partilederen for Cockroach Janta ble arrestert, og andre partiledere ble fengslet for brudd på forbudet mot proteststedet, noe som viser pågående undertrykkelse av dissent. I Haryana ble to personer pågrepet for angivelig å ha angrepet en buss på vei til Srinagar, noe som førte til fordømmelse fra kashmir-ledere. I Manipur kunngjorde Kuki-militante en nedstengning av en viktig motorvei etter angrep på landsbyer, femten hus ble satt i brann i Kamjong-distrikt, og én person ble drept i sammenstøt i Thoubal-distrikt, med påbud om nattlys. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
